minutes.headline: Conservation Commission continued the Richie screen-porch request to April 19 pending drywell and dimension plans.
minutes.summary: Commission met by Zoom. It approved two small gift/timber-fund expenditures for Earth Day, heard a resident about a shed encroaching on conservation land, and held a public hearing on an amended order of conditions for a screened porch at 137 Flynn Road. Members wanted documented dimensions and drainage plans, so the hearing was continued. Also discussed: encroachments, Table Rock trails, a certificate of compliance, and continued Zoom meetings.

Shed on 950 Chase Road reported as encroaching on conservation land; residents say it predates them and they don't use it, and they gave permission to cross their property to remove it.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission continued the amended order of conditions hearing for a screened porch at 137 Flynn Road to April 19.
Members asked the applicants to email an aerial plan showing exact porch dimensions, stairs and drywell location and volume two weeks ahead of the next hearing.
The commission approved two small expenditures for Earth Day, one from the Haas gift fund and one from the Timber rights fund, and approved a certificate of compliance.
The chair will consult the town attorney about a shed reported to encroach on conservation land at 950 Chase Road.

why_it_matters: Work near wetlands on Flynn Road stays under review until drainage and dimensions are documented, so the porch cannot proceed under the amended order before April 19 at the earliest.
Small Earth Day costs came from the commission's gift and timber-rights funds, not the tax-funded budget, and the encroachment question may affect how conservation land boundaries are enforced.
watch_next: April 19 continued hearing on the Richie amended order of conditions, with the aerial plan due two weeks beforehand.
Follow-up email from the chair after consulting the town attorney on the 950 Chase Road shed.
